skill.name: file-path-traversal-testing
skill.description: Assess authorized web applications for path traversal risks, including file-parameter discovery, safe proof collection, impact analysis, and remediation planning.
skill.summary: Guide authorized path traversal assessment, impact evidence, and remediation planning.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are confirmed because the skill teaches actionable path traversal exploitation, sensitive file targeting, and LFI-to-RCE escalation. Markdown backtick detections are false positives, but the remaining confirmed findings show critical risk and unsafe marketplace content.

remediation.suggestion: Rewrite the skill for authorized defensive validation, remove exploit-first language, and add clear refusal boundaries for unsanctioned targets.
Remove SSH keys, password files, registry hives, and credential-bearing paths. Use synthetic canary files or lab-only examples instead.
Remove log poisoning, PHP wrapper execution, and command execution payloads. Describe escalation impact at a high level only.
Limit examples to local lab hosts or clearly scoped assets, and add rate limits plus stop conditions for every workflow.
Require redaction, minimal proof collection, and immediate stopping when secret material appears during testing.

content.value_statement: Path traversal bugs can expose server files and credentials. This skill gives authorized testers a structured workflow for finding, proving, and reporting them.
actual_capabilities: Identifies file-handling parameters that may accept user-controlled paths.
Provides Linux and Windows traversal payload families, including encoded variants.
Shows authorized testing workflows with browser tools, Burp Suite, curl, ffuf, and wfuzz.
Explains impact evidence for readable system, process, web server, and application files.
Includes remediation patterns using whitelists, canonical paths, and base directory checks.
limitations: Requires clear authorization and a defined testing scope before use.
Does not verify ownership, legal authorization, or business impact by itself.
Some payloads depend on specific frameworks, permissions, and legacy parser behavior.
Contains offensive examples that are unsafe for public or unsanctioned targets.

use_cases.title: Validate File Download Controls
use_cases.description: Assess whether a scoped web endpoint can read files outside its intended directory.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Penetration Test Finding
use_cases.description: Organize evidence, impact, and remediation notes for a confirmed traversal issue.

use_cases.title: Review Path Handling Fixes
use_cases.description: Compare mitigations such as whitelists and canonical paths against common bypass patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Check
prompt_templates.prompt: I have authorization to test one file download endpoint. Help me plan safe path traversal checks without accessing sensitive data.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Test Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scoped path traversal test matrix for Linux and Windows targets, with expected signals and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these authorized test observations and help decide whether they prove traversal impact without exposing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Write the Finding
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a professional vulnerability report with impact, affected parameters, reproduction summary, risk, and remediation guidance.

output_examples.input: A tester asks for a scoped plan for a download endpoint.
output_examples.output: A phased checklist covering authorization, parameter mapping, harmless canary tests, response comparison, stop conditions, and reporting notes.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to fix unsafe file path handling.
output_examples.output: A remediation summary recommending strict allowlists, canonical path checks, fixed base directories, and tests for encoded traversal variants.

output_examples.input: A security lead asks for evidence handling guidance.
output_examples.output: A concise policy for minimizing sensitive data collection, redacting proof, preserving request metadata, and escalating only within written scope.

best_practices: Confirm written permission and scope before testing any target.
Use harmless canary files or lab systems when proving access.
Stop testing when secret material appears and document only necessary evidence.
anti_patterns: Collecting or publishing passwords, private keys, tokens, or registry hives.
Using RCE escalation as routine proof when file read evidence is enough.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It should only be used on systems where the tester has explicit written permission.

faq.question: Can it prove impact without reading secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. Use harmless canary files, metadata, or controlled lab fixtures whenever possible.

faq.question: Does it perform automated exploitation itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides testing guidance and command examples, but the operator controls all actions.

faq.question: Which tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references browser tools, Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, curl, ffuf, wfuzz, and traversal wordlists.

faq.question: How should sensitive findings be reported?
faq.answer: Report the minimum proof needed, redact secret values, and follow the engagement disclosure process.

faq.question: Can developers use it defensively?
faq.answer: Yes. Developers can use the prevention section to review validation, allowlists, and canonical path checks.
